disease_label_per_paper: Full axial spinal epidural abscess caused by community-acquired ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae with admission blood and urine gram-negative bacilli
presentation_summary: 55-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes presented with fever, dysuria, malaise, urinary incontinence, and worsening back pain causing difficulty ambulating for one week.
Initial vital signs showed temperature 38.3 degC, BP 186/82 mmHg, pulse 114/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Labs showed WBC 15.6 x10^9/L with 87% neutrophils; comprehensive metabolic panel and coagulation studies were reported as unremarkable without exact numeric values.
Neurologic deterioration led to MRI showing extensive posterior epidural fluid collection with internal air locules from C1 to L4, mass effect on the cord, and severe thecal sac stenosis.
Admission blood and urine cultures initially showed gram-negative bacilli; final blood, urine, and abscess cultures isolated ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.

quality_warnings: This case is a post-microbiology ESBL bacteremia test: blood culture gram-negative bacteremia, ESBL phenotype, ceftriaxone non-susceptibility, and carbapenem susceptibility are rankable because they define the resistance leaf.
Treatment response remains non-ranking confirmatory evidence; spinal epidural abscess features are preserved because they drive source-control need.
